concepts.why: Hypertension was first noted at age 24 during pregnancy and was controlled on a single antihypertensive agent.
The patient had normochromic microcytic anemia on full blood examination.
The patient had thrombocytopenia on full blood examination.
The patient had a basal ganglia hemorrhage and a history of hypertension.
The patient had bilateral adrenal lesions with no symptoms of adrenal hormone excess.
The patient had hepatosplenomegaly and a history of splenomegaly of unknown cause.
The patient had a history of splenomegaly of unknown cause and a younger brother with a similar finding.
The patient had low HDL and elevated triglycerides on lipid profile.

rationales.F02: Hypertension at a young age suggests primary hypertension.
rationales.F03: Basal ganglia hemorrhage is a common presentation of hypertensive intracranial hemorrhage.
rationales.F05: Family history of splenomegaly suggests a familial component.
rationales.F06: Normochromic microcytic anemia is a distinct finding.
rationales.F08: Dyslipidemia is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
rationales.F09: Bilateral adrenal lesions are suggestive of non-functioning adrenal adenoma.
rationales.F11: Absence of symptoms of adrenal hormone excess makes non-functioning adrenal adenoma more likely.
rationales.F12: Controlled blood pressure on a single antihypertensive agent suggests mild hypertension.
